natural_question.query_form_basis: the question text verbatim — what query.py sends as situation.question

summary.search_scope: every gold question, routed ones included; the metrics above are the search harness and nothing else

questions.page_rank_basis: not reported: this interface answers with documents, not pages

routed.comparability: answer_support is the graded number: the annotated answer terms in the text of the ONE document the interface asserts as its answer -- the active member for `resolve`, the top-ranked fact's document for `facts`. It is narrower than page_evidence_support (a document, not a page) and wider than evidence_support (a document, not a unit), so it is the analogue of neither and must not be averaged with either. returned_documents_support is the same terms anywhere in ANY document returned -- for `resolve` that is the whole supersession chain, so a term printed only in a superseded member counts. It is reported and never graded. page_rank is reported only where the interface knows a page; `resolve` answers with documents and reports none. The pass rule is the search harness's own, applied to answer_support. These numbers are NOT part of the headline metrics and are not averaged into them.
